svg.text: The home visit: the only place you see the cause
A clinic shows you the illness. The house shows you why it keeps coming back.
The order of a visit
1. Prepare
2. Greet
3. Observe
4. Provide
5. Teach
6. Record
Review the record before you go. Greet the household head. Never begin with instructions.
What to look at without being asked
Where the drinking water is kept, and covered
Whether there is a latrine, and if it is used
Bed nets — hanging, or folded in a corner
Where food is stored and how it is covered
Standing water in tyres, tins and pots
Who else in the house is coughing
Smoke from cooking inside the room
How to teach so it is actually done
Agree one change, not seven
Use what the household already owns
Demonstrate; then let them do it while you watch
Ask them to explain it back to you
Speak to whoever actually decides
Advice that costs money the family has not got
is not advice. It is a way of blaming them.
Why families default, and what actually works
They cannot pay ....................... check NHIS status, exemptions, and the real cost of transport
It is too far ............................. outreach, or a visit timed to a market day
Someone at home forbids it ........ speak with that person, not around him
They were treated badly last time .. this is the commonest reason and the least often recorded
They believe it did not work ........ ask what they expected it to do
Never open with a scolding. A mother who is shamed once does not come back a second time.
Find the reason before you supply the solution — the reason is almost never that she does not care.
